FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: misir wat
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: red {0_coll} melted down in a spiced butter and a mixture of {1_adj}, until they form nothing but a dark purée. Eaten without utensils, pinched up in a spongy flatbread.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichokes vinaigrette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} boiled whole and head down, served warm with a mustard vinaigrette. You pull the leaves off one by one and scrape the base of each between your teeth; the heart is kept for last.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed artichokes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cleared of their choke, filled with a {1_adj} stuffing bound with crumb, and braised upright in a little stock until the leaves open of their own accord.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carciofi alla romana
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} trimmed down to the tender heart, stuffed with {1_plur} and Roman mint, planted stem upwards in a narrow pan and sweated in oil and water.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carciofi alla giudia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} whole fried twice over, crushed between the two fryings so that the leaves open into a flower and turn as brittle as crisps. An invention of the Roman ghetto.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichoke pizza
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated in oil and laid on the base at the last moment, with {1_coll} — one of the four quarters of a capricciosa, promoted to a whole dish.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: asparagus à la flamande
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: white {0_coll} served with a hard-boiled egg crushed with a fork into melted butter, parsley and a grating of nutmeg. Everyone mixes their own sauce on their own plate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: asparagus tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} laid out in spokes over a blind-baked base, with a {1_adj} cream between them. Tips to the centre, ends to the rim: that is the only way every slice gets one.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: brussels sprout curry
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} quartered and stewed in a {1_adj} milk built on cumin, turmeric and mustard seeds burst in hot oil.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pear and gorgonzola pizza
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a white base with no tomato, {1_coll} in drops and {0_coll} in slices laid on halfway through the baking so that they do not dry out, with a thread of honey as it comes out.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fig and goat's cheese crostini
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: slices of toasted bread, fresh {1_coll} crushed over them and {0_coll} opened in four, run under the grill for thirty seconds. The honey goes on after, never before.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: apple and cheddar toastie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: aged {1_coll} and {0_coll} in fine slivers between two buttered slices, pressed in the pan. The apple gives up a little water that keeps the cheese from setting.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hot goat's cheese with cherries
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a round of {1_adj} set on a slice of bread and put in the oven until it runs, with {0_coll} fried in vinegar. The acidity of the fruit cuts the fat of the hot cheese.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cheese-stuffed mushrooms
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} destalked and filled with a {1_adj} stuffing and breadcrumbs, baked until they give up their water and take it back again.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: saganaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick slice of hard {0_adj} floured and seared in a small two-handled pan, until a crust forms. Doused with {1_plur} at the table, and sometimes flamed.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ricotta and spinach gnudi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the filling of a ravioli without its wrapper — {0_coll} and {1_coll} bound with a little flour and poached naked. Gnudi means undressed.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: grilled halloumi with vegetables
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sliced thick and grilled until it takes the bars without melting — it is the only cheese that holds on a grill — with roasted {1_coll} and za'atar.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: xiaolongbao
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: dumplings pleated eighteen times, filled with {1_plur} and a jelly of stock that turns back to liquid in the steam. You pierce them before biting, on pain of a burn.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: xiaolongbao
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: dumplings pleated eighteen times, filled with {0_plur} and a jelly of stock that turns back to liquid in the steam. You pierce them before biting, on pain of a burn.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: wonton
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: squares of dough so fine that the {0_adj} filling shows through, closed with a pinch and poached in a {1_adj} broth. The tail of dough floats and ripples: that is what gave them their name.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: peking duck
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bird blown full of air to lift the skin off the flesh, scalded, lacquered with {1_plur} and dried a day in the wind before roasting. The skin is served first, in fine pancakes, and the meat afterwards.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bœuf miroton
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the {0_adj} left over from the pot-au-feu, sliced and reheated in a {1_adj} sauce with vinegar and mustard. A dish born of thrift and kept on for the taste of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tongue in sauce piquante
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached for hours then peeled while still hot — cold, the skin will not come away — served under a {1_adj} sauce with vinegar and gherkins.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tête de veau sauce gribiche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} rolled and poached in a white broth, served warm under a sauce built on hard-boiled {1_adj} yolks, lifted with capers and herbs. You either eat it or you do not; there is no middle ground.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tablier de sapeur
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a piece of {0_adj} marinated in white wine, crumbed with {1_plur} and breadcrumbs, then grilled. The name comes from a marshal of Lyon who had been a sapper in his youth.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: andouillette and chips
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an andouillette grilled until the skin splits open, with {1_coll} in batons and a spoonful of mustard. You either love it or you leave the table.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: palette à la diable
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: smoked {0_coll} poached, painted over with {1_plur} and breadcrumbs, then run under the grill until it crusts. À la diable means only this: mustarded and scalding.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ham on the bone
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole piece of {0_adj} cooked on its bone and carved in front of you. The flesh against the bone is the best of it, and the last to be served.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} shank
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the small muscle of the shank, braised so long that it slides off the bone. One shank a guest, never fewer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} shank
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the small muscle of the shank, braised so long that it slides off the bone. One shank a guest, never fewer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed cabbage
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole cabbage blanched and opened leaf by leaf, packed with {1_plur} between every layer, then closed up in a cloth and poached for hours. It is cut into wedges, like a cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: croque-madame
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a croque-monsieur crowned with a fried egg, whose broken yolk serves as the sauce. The hat is what earns it the name.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: onion tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed an hour without taking any colour, mixed with smoked {1_plur} and spread over a shortcrust base. Alsatian or Lyonnais, according to the hand that made it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pâté en croûte
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a stuffing of {0_adj} and {1_adj} built into a terrine of pastry, baked with a chimney, then filled with jelly through that hole once it has cooled. Cut clean, cold, never warm.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vol-au-vent
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a puff pastry case so light it might fly away — hence the name — filled with {0_adj} and {1_adj} in a white sauce, and re-hatted with its own lid.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pound cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: as much flour as {0_adj}, as sugar, as {1_adj} — four equal quarters, which is what the French name says. You weigh the eggs first and everything else follows.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: yoghurt cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the {0_adj} pot serves as the measure for everything else. The first cake anyone learns to make, and the only one whose recipe is never forgotten.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: paris-brest
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a ring of choux pastry split and filled with a {0_adj} praline cream. The shape imitates a bicycle wheel: the pastrycook had his shop on the route of the race.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mille-feuille
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: three sheets of puff pastry baked under a weight to stay flat, built up with a {1_adj} pastry cream. Eaten lying on its side: nobody has ever managed it any other way.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coffee éclair
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a length of choux pastry filled with a {0_adj} cream and iced in the same flavour. The name is said to come from how fast it is eaten.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rum baba
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a risen dough dried out on purpose, then drowned in a warm {1_adj} syrup with {0_plur} until it can take up no more. Pressed gently, it should give juice back.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: profiteroles
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small choux buns filled with {1_adj} ice cream, drowned under hot {0_coll} poured in front of the guests. The clash of temperatures is the whole dessert.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: madeleines
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a batter rested in the cold then put into a very hot oven: the thermal shock makes the hump, and a madeleine without a hump has failed. Scented with {1_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: canelés
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a liquid batter rested two days, baked in copper moulds lined with wax, until an almost black crust forms around a soft {0_adj} and {1_adj} heart.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Breton shortbread
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: almost as much salted {0_adj} as flour, barely worked so it stays sandy. The salt is not a seasoning here: it is the main ingredient after the butter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: teurgoule
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} with cinnamon, baked five hours in the baker's oven in an earthenware dish, until a thick brown skin forms. The name comes from the burn it deals to anyone who will not wait.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bugnes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: ribbons of knotted dough, scented with {1_plur} and orange flower water, fried and sugared. Thick in Lyon, dry and brittle in Saint-Étienne: each city defends its own.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sachertorte
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dense {0_adj} sponge, split and filled with a layer of {1_adj} jam, glazed with a dark smooth fondant. Two Viennese houses spent seven years in court over this cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: apfelstrudel
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough stretched by hand over a tablecloth until a newspaper can be read through it, filled with {0_adj} and dried {1_adj}, then rolled. One tear in the dough and it all begins again.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kaiserschmarrn
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick {0_adj} pancake torn into pieces with the spatula while it cooks, caramelised in sugar with dried {1_coll}. The Emperor's mess: the name admits its want of manners.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: makowiec
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a brioche rolled over a mass of ground poppy seeds cooked with {1_plur}. The black and white spiral shows at the cut.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: medovik
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dozen discs of {0_adj} dough baked one at a time, stacked with a soured cream and left overnight so the whole thing softens and turns tender.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bakewell tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a shortcrust base, a layer of {1_adj} jam, and an {0_adj} frangipane over the top that rises and browns in the oven.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tres leches
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a sponge dried out on purpose, pricked all over and drowned in three different milks until it can take no more. It has to be sodden without collapsing: that is the whole exercise.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: alfajores
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: two very short biscuits stuck together with dulce de leche, the edges rolled in grated {1_plur}. They fall apart the moment you pick them up, which is the sign they are good.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: brownie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: very little flour, a great deal of {0_adj}, and crushed {1_coll}. Out of the oven too late and it is only a cake; too early and it is not yet a brownie.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cheesecake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a base of buttered biscuits under an {0_adj} and {1_adj} filling, baked in a water bath and cooled slowly — a shock of temperature splits it in two.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lamington
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of sponge dipped in a runny {0_adj} icing then rolled in grated {1_plur}. Australian, and named after a governor of Queensland who had nothing to do with it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: malva pudding
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a South African {0_adj} and apricot cake, pricked as it leaves the oven and drowned in a hot {1_adj} sauce that it absorbs entirely.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: künefe
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: fresh {0_coll} caught between two layers of shredded pastry, browned on both sides then doused in scalding syrup. Eaten at once: the cheese must still pull.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: maamoul
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a semolina worked with clarified {1_plur} and rested overnight, filled with {0_plur} and pressed into a carved wooden mould. Each pattern names a different filling.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: om ali
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: broken puff pastry drowned in sweetened {0_plur} and covered with {1_adj}, browned until the top crisps over a sodden underside.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: basbousa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a semolina cake with {0_adj} and {1_adj}, cut into diamonds before baking and soaked with syrup the moment it leaves the oven, while it is still scalding.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: taiyaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a waffle batter cooked in a mould shaped like a sea bream, filled with a sweet {0_adj} paste. Whether to bite the head or the tail first divides Japan.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hotteok
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a risen flatbread filled with cane {0_plur} and crushed {1_plur}, flattened on the hot plate. The filling turns into a boiling syrup that burns the tongue without fail.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bánh pía sầu riêng
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Vietnamese cake of spiralled puff pastry, filled with a paste of {0_adj} and a salted {1_adj} yolk at the centre. The layers peel apart one by one at the cut.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian mooncake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an uncooked snow-skin dough pressed in a seal, filled with the flesh of {0_adj} and a sweetened {1_adj} paste. Served iced, unlike the classic mooncake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian mille crêpes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: twenty very fine pancakes stacked up, each parted from the next by a layer of {0_adj} flesh folded into whipped {1_plur}. Cut clean, and eaten iced.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian puff
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small choux buns filled with a pure {0_adj} cream, served cold. Sold in refrigerated boxes in Singapore, and banned on the underground like everything else containing that fruit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very airy sponge into whose raw batter the flesh of {0_adj} is folded. The smell fills the kitchen while it bakes and settles there for the day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tempoyak
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the flesh of {0_adj} salted and left to ferment a week in a closed jar, until it turns sour and creamy. It is no longer a fruit at that stage: it is a condiment, and it keeps for months.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vareniki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: half-moons of dough filled with crushed {0_plur}, poached and then doused with {1_adj} melted down in butter. The seal has to hold in boiling water: that is the whole craft.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: khachapuri
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bread shaped like a boat filled with melted {0_adj}, with a raw yolk and a knob of {1_adj} set at the centre as it leaves the oven. Everything is mixed together with the tip of the crust, torn off for the purpose.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: francesinha
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Porto croque-monsieur pushed to absurdity: four meats stacked, melted cheese over the top, and a thick {1_adj} and tomato sauce poured to the brim of the plate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bifana
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: thin {0_adj} escalopes simmered with {1_plur} and white wine, stacked scalding into a roll that drinks up the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cataplana de marisco
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} cooked together in a hinged copper pot clamped shut — no steam escapes, and the dish cooks in its own juices.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sauerbraten
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a joint of {0_adj} marinated in vinegar for a whole week, braised, the sauce thickened with crumbled gingerbread and sweetened with dried {1_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: schweinshaxe
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole knuckle roasted for hours and basted with brown {1_plur}, until the rind becomes a shell that cracks under the knife.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: wiener schnitzel
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an escalope of {0_adj} beaten until translucent, crumbed without pressing, and fried in butter with the pan shaken so the coating puffs and lifts off the meat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tafelspitz
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a cut of {0_adj} poached in a broth of roots, served with an {1_adj} sauce of horseradish and apple. Franz Joseph's favourite dish, they say, and he ate it every day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: frikadeller
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} minced twice, lightened with flour and {1_adj}, shaped with a spoon into domed patties and fried long and slow in butter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lapskaus
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and the roots cooked together so long that nothing can be told apart. A sailor's dish, made of salted meat and whatever kept on board.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: steak and ale pie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in brown {1_plur} until it falls into threads, shut in under a pastry lid that swells and browns in the oven.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kedgeree
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: curried {0_coll} folded through flaked smoked fish and hard-boiled eggs. An Indian khichdi carried home by the British and turned by them into a breakfast dish.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fig tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} split in a cross and stood upright on a {1_adj} cream, which drinks up their juice as it bakes and keeps the pastry from going soft.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: crostata di fichi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a shortcrust made with {1_plur}, crossed into a lattice over a thick layer of {0_adj} jam. Eaten cold, the next day, once the pastry has drunk a little of the fruit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fig focaccia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} pushed down into dough dimpled with the fingers, with rosemary, {1_adj} oil and coarse salt. The sugar of the fruit caramelises where it touches the tray.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fig and prosciutto pizza
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a white base with no tomato, {0_coll} roasted on it, and raw {1_coll} laid on only as it leaves the oven — cooked, it hardens and loses everything.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lamb and fig tagine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} stewed with saffron, ginger and cinnamon, dried {0_coll} swelled back up and added at the end with toasted almonds.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pissaladière
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Niçois tart: {0_coll} stewed a whole hour until they are almost a jam, spread over the dough and latticed with {1_adj}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fondue savoyarde
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted in {1_plur} in a pot rubbed with garlic, kept hot the whole evening. Bread is dipped in on the end of a fork; whoever drops it buys the next round.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: aligot
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mash of {0_adj} worked with {1_plur} and a spatula, for a long time, until it draws into ribbons when it is lifted. The arm gives out before the paste does.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: flammekueche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough rolled out to the very edge of tearing, covered with raw {0_adj} and {1_adj}, slid for two minutes as close to the embers as it will go.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kougelhopf
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a slow brioche baked in a fluted mould, with {0_plur} soaked in advance and {1_plur} set in the bottom so that they end up at the summit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: far breton
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dense custard of {0_plur} and {1_plur}, baked until the top browns and the middle still trembles.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} confit
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} salted for a day, then cooked very slowly submerged in {1_plur}, and kept in it afterwards. The skin is crisped at the last moment, in a pan.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} blanquette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked without taking any colour — that is the whole difficulty — the sauce mounted with {1_plur} and sharpened at the very last moment.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gratinée onion soup
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} browned very slowly to a deep colour, moistened, then covered with bread and {1_adj} and run under the grill.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: croque-monsieur
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: two slices of bread, {1_coll} between them, {0_coll} above and below, the whole browned until the edges run over and catch a little.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: leek flamiche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted in {1_plur} without colour, shut between two sheets of pastry and baked until the top gilds. Picard, and with no cream at all in the original.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pigs' trotters Sainte-Menehould
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: trotters poached for forty hours, until the bones turn tender and are eaten along with the rest, then crumbed and grilled. Louis XVI is said to have stopped for them during his flight, which delayed him.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: baked camembert
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole box of {0_adj} scored in a cross, stuck with {1_plur} and put into the oven in its own wood until it runs. Bread is dipped into it until there is nothing left.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: omelette de la Mère Poulard
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} beaten very long with a whisk, until they foam like a soufflé, and cooked in {1_plur} in a long-handled pan over a wood fire. The exact recipe was never given away.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: scallops à la bretonne
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} put back into its shell under garlic and parsley and breadcrumbs in {1_plur}, run under the grill for two minutes. Any longer and it turns to rubber.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: galette-saucisse
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a grilled sausage rolled in a cold {0_adj} galette, and nothing else — mustard is tolerated, ketchup is disputed. Eaten standing, at the match or at the market.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed clams
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} opened and covered with a butter worked with {1_plur} and parsley, put into the oven until the butter bubbles up and runs over the edge.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed spider crab
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} picked out patiently, mixed with its own coral and the yolks of hard-boiled {1_adj}, then packed back into the emptied shell. An hour of work for ten minutes of eating.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rillettes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked five hours in {1_coll} until it falls apart, pulled with a fork and never ground, then pressed into a pot under a layer of fat that keeps it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Easter pâté
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a stuffing of {0_adj} shut inside a pastry, with whole hard-boiled eggs lined up down the middle so that a yellow disc appears in every slice.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poulet en barbouille
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in wine, the sauce thickened with the bird's own blood and liver. Barbouille, for what it leaves on the chin of whoever eats it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: potée lorraine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and the roots of winter stewed together with smoked and salted {1_coll}. The broth is served first, over bread; the meats come afterwards.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: salade lyonnaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: bitter frisée, {1_coll} fried in the pan, croutons rubbed with garlic and a poached egg set over the top. You break the yolk and it becomes the dressing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: biryani
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} half-cooked and marinated {1_coll} built up in layers, sealed under a lid luted with dough, and finished smothered. It is never stirred: every layer must still be distinct when it is opened.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: palak paneer
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} blanched then ground into a green purée kept brief so as not to brown, into which are set cubes of fresh {1_adj} that do not melt.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gulab jamun
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} reduced for hours into a solid paste, rolled into balls, fried very gently, and left to drink up a {1_adj} syrup scented with rose. They have to run when you bite them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: risi e bisi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} cooked together, somewhere between a soup and a risotto — loose enough for the spoon, too thick for the bowl. The pods go into the stock; nothing is wasted.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gnocchi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} crushed while still hot and bound with as little flour as can be managed, rolled, and ridged with a fork. They are done when they rise.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: focaccia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very wet dough dimpled with the fingertips, drowned in {1_adj} oil and salted in coarse grains. The holes hold the oil: they are not decorative.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: caprese
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} in alternating slices, oil, salt, green leaves. Nothing else, and above all no vinegar.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: saltimbocca
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an escalope of {0_adj} flattened out, a sage leaf and a slice of {1_adj} pinned to it, seared a minute a side. The name says: leaps into the mouth.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: udon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: thick, soft noodles kneaded underfoot beneath a cloth, in a clear {1_adj} broth. The texture matters more than the taste, and it is deliberate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: soba
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: grey {0_adj} noodles, served cold on a rack with a {1_adj} sauce apart. The cooking water is drunk at the end, let down in what is left of the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: agedashi dofu
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {0_adj} tofu rolled in starch and fried, set into a warm {1_adj} broth. The crust holds just long enough to reach the table.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: korokke
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mash of {0_adj} mixed with minced {1_plur}, crumbed in coarse breadcrumbs and fried. A distant descendant of the French croquette, which arrived by boat last century.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: dorayaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: two small thick pancakes made with {1_plur} and honey, closed over a sweet {0_adj} paste. The name comes from the gong they imitate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pajeon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick pancake in which {1_coll} stand upright in the batter, gilded on both sides in generous oil. Eaten on rainy days: the sound of the frying recalls the sound of the drops.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fattoush
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: stale flatbread, toasted and broken by hand, thrown over {0_coll} and {1_coll} with sumac. Served at the last moment: the bread must still crack.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tabbouleh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mountain of herbs chopped by knife, {1_coll} in dice, and only a handful of bulgur. The version in which the grain dominates is an invention from elsewhere.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tabbouleh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mountain of herbs chopped by knife, {0_coll} in dice, and only a handful of bulgur. The version in which the grain dominates is an invention from elsewhere.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pastilla
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} pulled into threads and toasted {1_coll} shut inside sheets of warqa, the whole dusted over with sugar and cinnamon. A savoury dish served under a sweet layer, and nobody finds it strange.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: briouates
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: triangles of warqa filled with pounded {0_plur}, fried and then plunged scalding into cold honey. The shock of temperature is what makes them crisp.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mint tea
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: green {0_coll}, a handful of mint, and a great deal more {1_adj} than anyone likes to admit. Poured from a height to raise the foam, and three times rather than once.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: royal couscous
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: semolina rolled by hand and steamed three times over the broth, served with {0_plur} and {1_plur}. The grain never touches the water.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: seffa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: steamed semolina heaped into a cone, striped with cinnamon and icing sugar, crowned with fried {0_plur}, with {1_plur} served apart and cold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: msemen
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough stretched to transparency on an oiled surface, brushed with {0_plur} and semolina, folded into a square and folded again, then cooked dry. The layers are counted when it is torn.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: aamras
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the pulp of {0_adj} pressed out by hand rather than blended — the whisk oxidises it and dulls the colour — with barely any {1_plur}, scented with cardamom and saffron.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: aamras puri
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the purée of {0_adj} served with scalding puffed puri, torn open to dip with. Sweet and savoury in the same mouthful: a whole meal in Gujarat while the season lasts.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mango float
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: alternating layers of graham crackers, {1_adj} whipped with condensed milk and {0_adj} in slivers, left overnight in the cold to set. The biscuits soften and turn into cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: green mango curry
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: green {0_coll} stewed in a {1_adj} milk raised with turmeric and mustard seed. The fruit keeps its shape and its acidity: this is not a dessert, whatever sugar it holds.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chicken and mango curry
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} stewed in a sauce where ripe {0_coll} melts away and sweetens the curry, while a few green pieces kept whole supply the acid.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ghee rice
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: basmati {0_coll} turned in clarified {1_coll} with whole spices — cinnamon, clove, cardamom, bay — then swelled in boiling water. Called neychoru in Kerala, where it goes with the feasts.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coconut chutney
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} blended with toasted {1_coll} and a little water, then woken up with a tempering: mustard seed and curry leaves burst in scalding oil and poured over the top. It goes with the dosa.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: picarones
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: rings of {0_adj} and sweet potato dough, shaped by hand with a turning gesture, fried and drowned in a dark {1_adj} syrup. The colonial successor of an older fritter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: narsharab
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the Azerbaijani molasses, mounted with {1_plur} and scented with cinnamon, clove and bay. Served with grilled sturgeon, and nothing else will stand in for it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pomegranate fattoush
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: flatbread fried and broken up, {1_coll} and herbs, with a dressing of sumac and {0_adj} molasses. The bread must still crack when it reaches the table.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kısır with pomegranate
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: fine bulgur swelled in hot water and worked by hand with {1_adj} concentrate, mild pepper and {0_adj} molasses. Served in leaves of lettuce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lamb and pomegranate tagine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} stewed with saffron and cinnamon, the sauce sharpened with the juice of {0_adj} and the fresh seeds sown on only as it is served — cooked, they lose everything.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: anardana chutney
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the dried and ground seeds of wild {0_adj}, pounded with green {1_plur} and coriander. Anardana stands in for tamarind across the whole of northern India.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: anardana chicken
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} marinated in the ground seeds of {0_adj}, whose acidity tenderises the flesh, then stewed with dry spices, with neither tomato nor yoghurt.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: prickly pear tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a shortcrust base made with {1_plur}, filled with a set {0_adj} jelly whose colour goes from magenta to garnet as it cools.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sashimi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw and sliced in one drawn stroke, never sawn, on a bed of shredded radish. The knife and the angle of the cut make the whole dish; there is nothing else to be done.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gored gored
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw in cubes rather than chopped, rolled in a spiced butter and awaze. The kitfo's cousin in pieces, and the most merciless test of freshness there is.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meat sausage
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} minced twice, let down with crumb and heavily {1_plur}, cased and then poached. The mincer settles the question of texture.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meat pie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in advance and shut under a {1_adj} pastry. What is under the crust can no longer be seen, and that is part of the point.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: soda-glazed pork
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a ham cooked slowly in sweetened {0_coll}, whose sugar caramelises and whose acid tenderises. A recipe out of a tin-can kitchen, and nobody has ever explained why it works.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: alligator sauce piquante
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} from the tail in dice, stewed in a roux and {1_coll} with cayenne pepper. The Cajun alligator dish, the one served at the parish fairs.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cajun alligator bites
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: dice of {0_adj} marinated in buttermilk, rolled in a {1_adj} flour with paprika and cayenne, and fried on the spot. Eaten on a toothpick, with a rémoulade.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: monitor lizard in coconut milk
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} jointed and stewed a long while in a spiced {1_adj} milk — its flesh is firm and lean, and gives way only over a low flame.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fried snake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: lengths of {0_adj} rolled in a seasoned flour and fried in {1_plur} to a gold. You eat around the ribs, as you would a corn cob.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tuwo dawa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the Hausa version: a {0_adj} ball moulded with a ladle, with a miyan kuka of pounded baobab leaves and a {1_adj} sauce. Baobab thickens without any flour at all.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sorghum genfo
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very thick {0_adj} porridge moulded into a dome, hollowed at the centre and filled with niter kibbeh — a clarified butter with spices — and {1_adj} berbere. The lunch of young Ethiopian mothers.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: popped sorghum
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} thrown by the handful into a scorching pan: the grains burst into minute white balls, ten times smaller than popcorn, and a great deal more tender.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gỏi cuốn
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_adj} wrappers dipped a second into warm water, rolled tight over {1_coll} and herbs. You can see the pink through the sheet: that is why it is rolled that way round.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bo bun
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cold {0_adj} vermicelli under scalding fried {1_coll}, with raw herbs and a clear sweet-salt sauce poured over the top. Hot and cold in the same bowl, and it is not a fault.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: nem
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: fine rolls filled with minced {0_plur} and black {1_plur} soaked back up, fried twice over. Eaten wrapped in a lettuce leaf, with mint.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pulpo a la gallega
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} dipped three times into boiling water before it is left there — otherwise the skin comes away — cut with scissors over rounds of {1_adj}, oil and smoked paprika.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fabada
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: large white beans stewed with smoked {1_plur}, never stirred with a spoon: the pot is shaken with a turn of the wrist so as not to break them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: salmorejo
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} ground with crumb and mounted with oil into an orange cream thick enough to stand up, served iced with hard-boiled {1_coll} crumbled over. Denser than gazpacho, of which it is the Córdoban cousin.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fideuà
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: short hollow pasta toasted dry then cooked in a {1_adj} fumet, which they drink up while standing on end. Born of a ship's boy hiding the rice from a captain who ate too much of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: onion tatin
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} halved and set cut side down in a {1_adj} caramel with vinegar, covered over with pastry and turned out after baking. The principle of the apple tart, applied to the savoury.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cipolline in agrodolce
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small whole {0_coll} glazed in balsamic vinegar and {1_plur}, with bay. Eaten cold, and they keep a week, gaining by the day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sweet-and-sour beetroot
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked in their skins then marinated in a {1_adj} vinegar with mustard seed and dill. They take a week to come into balance and keep for months.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: takuan
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a daikon dried in the sun for weeks until it will bend, then buried in rice bran with {1_plur} and salt. Bright yellow, crisp, and loud to chew.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vegetable achards
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cut into fine julienne, blanched then drowned in an oil with turmeric, ginger and vinegar, with just enough {1_adj} to round off the acid. They improve over three days.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: khoresh-e beh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with quinces in quarters, whose hard flesh melts within the hour and scents everything, sharpened with verjuice and sweetened with a little honey.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: steamed pork with water chestnuts
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} chopped by knife and worked in one direction only until it turns elastic, {0_coll} in small dice through it, the whole spread into a cake and steamed over the rice.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pork and water chestnut dumplings
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {1_adj} stuffing in which chopped {0_coll} bring the crunch that meat alone never gives, shut inside discs of dough pleated by hand.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: prawn and water chestnut dumplings
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} left in large pieces rather than ground down, mixed with {0_plur} in dice. Two textures that crack, each in its own way.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: water chestnut spring rolls
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} and {0_coll} finely sliced, rolled tight in a sheet of pastry and fried to a golden brown. The crunch comes from the inside as much as from the crust.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichokes vinaigrette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} boiled whole and head down, served warm with a mustard vinaigrette. You pull the leaves off one by one and scrape the base of each between your teeth; the heart is kept for last.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carciofi alla giudia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} whole fried twice over, crushed between the two fryings so that the leaves open into a flower and turn as brittle as crisps. An invention of the Roman ghetto.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: asparagus à la flamande
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: white {0_coll} served with a hard-boiled egg crushed with a fork into melted butter, parsley and a grating of nutmeg. Everyone mixes their own sauce on their own plate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: asparagus with sauce mousseline
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the same hollandaise, lightened by a third with whipped cream folded in off the heat. It doubles in volume and loses its bite: the Sunday version.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ham on the bone
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole piece of {0_adj} cooked on its bone and carved in front of you. The flesh against the bone is the best of it, and the last to be served.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chocolate mousse
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted and bound with yolks, lightened with whipped whites folded in three goes — the first third to loosen it, the other two with a spatula, without knocking the air out.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: künefe
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: fresh {0_coll} caught between two layers of shredded pastry, browned on both sides then doused in scalding syrup. Eaten at once: the cheese must still pull.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian puff
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small choux buns filled with a pure {0_adj} cream, served cold. Sold in refrigerated boxes in Singapore, and banned on the underground like everything else containing that fruit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: durian cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very airy sponge into whose raw batter the flesh of {0_adj} is folded. The smell fills the kitchen while it bakes and settles there for the day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tempoyak
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the flesh of {0_adj} salted and left to ferment a week in a closed jar, until it turns sour and creamy. It is no longer a fruit at that stage: it is a condiment, and it keeps for months.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: wiener schnitzel
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an escalope of {0_adj} beaten until translucent, crumbed without pressing, and fried in butter with the pan shaken so the coating puffs and lifts off the meat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poronkäristys
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: reindeer {0_coll} planed into shavings off the frozen block, thrown into scalding fat and served with a mash and a spoonful of lingonberries. A dish of Lapland, eaten in winter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lapskaus
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and the roots cooked together so long that nothing can be told apart. A sailor's dish, made of salted meat and whatever kept on board.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kedgeree
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: curried {0_coll} folded through flaked smoked fish and hard-boiled eggs. An Indian khichdi carried home by the British and turned by them into a breakfast dish.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: daube provençale
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated a whole night, then cooked so long and so gently that it falls apart under the spoon.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gougères
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: choux pastry made with {0_plur}, puffed in the oven until it sounds hollow. Eaten warm, standing up, while waiting for the rest.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Easter pâté
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a stuffing of {0_adj} shut inside a pastry, with whole hard-boiled eggs lined up down the middle so that a yellow disc appears in every slice.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poulet en barbouille
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in wine, the sauce thickened with the bird's own blood and liver. Barbouille, for what it leaves on the chin of whoever eats it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gnocchi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} crushed while still hot and bound with as little flour as can be managed, rolled, and ridged with a fork. They are done when they rise.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: aamras puri
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the purée of {0_adj} served with scalding puffed puri, torn open to dip with. Sweet and savoury in the same mouthful: a whole meal in Gujarat while the season lasts.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pomegranate molasses
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the juice of {0_adj} reduced for hours to a tenth of its volume: thick, black and frankly sour. Dibs rumman in Arabic, nar ekşisi in Turkish — the lemon of the Levant.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: colonche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the juice of red {0_adj} left to ferment a few days in an earthenware jar. A pre-Hispanic drink, still sold in the markets of central Mexico.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sashimi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw and sliced in one drawn stroke, never sawn, on a bed of shredded radish. The knife and the angle of the cut make the whole dish; there is nothing else to be done.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gored gored
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw in cubes rather than chopped, rolled in a spiced butter and awaze. The kitfo's cousin in pieces, and the most merciless test of freshness there is.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: creole turtle soup
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in a brown roux with the Creole trinity, chopped hard-boiled eggs and a splash of sherry poured into the plate as it is served. The bottle stays on the table.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: popped sorghum
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} thrown by the handful into a scorching pan: the grains burst into minute white balls, ten times smaller than popcorn, and a great deal more tender.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: khoresh-e beh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with quinces in quarters, whose hard flesh melts within the hour and scents everything, sharpened with verjuice and sweetened with a little honey.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ma tai go
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a paste of {0_adj} starch and rock sugar, steamed into a translucent amber slab with whole dice set in it. Eaten warm, or cut up and fried in the pan the next day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: yoghurt cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the {0_adj} pot serves as the measure for everything else. The first cake anyone learns to make, and the only one whose recipe is never forgotten.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: medovik
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dozen discs of {0_adj} dough baked one at a time, stacked with a soured cream and left overnight so the whole thing softens and turns tender.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: taiyaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a waffle batter cooked in a mould shaped like a sea bream, filled with a sweet {0_adj} paste. Whether to bite the head or the tail first divides Japan.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: briouates
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: triangles of warqa filled with pounded {0_plur}, fried and then plunged scalding into cold honey. The shock of temperature is what makes them crisp.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pajeon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick pancake in which {0_coll} stand upright in the batter, gilded on both sides in generous oil. Eaten on rainy days: the sound of the frying recalls the sound of the drops.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: peking duck
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bird blown full of air to lift the skin off the flesh, scalded, lacquered with syrup and dried a day in the wind before roasting. The skin is served first, in fine pancakes, and the meat afterwards.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed cabbage
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole cabbage blanched and opened leaf by leaf, packed with meat between every layer, then closed up in a cloth and poached for hours. It is cut into wedges, like a cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sernik
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Polish curd cheese passed three times through a sieve, beaten with eggs and baked slowly. Denser and less sweet than its western cousins.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gravlax
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a fillet buried two days under salt, sugar and a great deal of dill, beneath a weight. The name means buried salmon: it really was once put down in the sand.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: eel in green sauce
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: lengths of eel poached in white wine in a mass of green herbs — sorrel, watercress, spinach — until the sauce takes their colour. Served cold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: marmite dieppoise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: several fish and shellfish poached separately and only then brought together in a broth creamed with cider. Every flesh has its own cooking time: put them all in at once and the whole thing is lost.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: duck à la rouennaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bird smothered rather than bled, so as to keep its blood, roasted rare; the carcass is then pressed and the juice bound with the liver and red wine.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: black pudding with apples
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a black pudding pricked with a fork and fried gently — too fierce a heat and it bursts — with apples caramelised in butter. The sugar of the fruit cuts the iron of the blood.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: salade lyonnaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: bitter frisée, lardons fried in the pan, croutons rubbed with garlic and a poached egg set over the top. You break the yolk and it becomes the dressing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poularde demi-deuil
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a fowl under whose skin black slivers of truffle have been slid, poached whole in a broth of bones. The black on the white is what earns it its name: half-mourning.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: focaccia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very wet dough dimpled with the fingertips, drowned in olive oil and salted in coarse grains. The holes hold the oil: they are not decorative.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: udon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: thick, soft noodles kneaded underfoot beneath a cloth, in a clear kombu broth. The texture matters more than the taste, and it is deliberate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: msemen
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough stretched to transparency on an oiled surface, brushed with butter and semolina, folded into a square and folded again, then cooked dry. The layers are counted when it is torn.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rice tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a very thick rice pudding poured into a case of plain risen dough, then baked until the top crazes over. The speciality of Verviers, eaten there for centuries.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: narsharab
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the Azerbaijani molasses, mounted with sugar and scented with cinnamon, clove and bay. Served with grilled sturgeon, and nothing else will stand in for it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pong tia koon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the Cambodian version, grilled over embers rather than boiled, served with a dip of lime, salt and Kampot pepper.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Chinese braised turtle
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a soft-shelled turtle braised in rice wine with black mushrooms, ginger and goji berries. The cartilage around the rim is the part sought after, gelatinous and melting.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fabada
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: large white beans stewed with smoked pork, never stirred with a spoon: the pot is shaken with a turn of the wrist so as not to break them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fideuà
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: short hollow pasta toasted dry then cooked in a fish fumet, which they drink up while standing on end. Born of a ship's boy hiding the rice from a captain who ate too much of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: takuan
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a daikon dried in the sun for weeks until it will bend, then buried in rice bran with sugar and salt. Bright yellow, crisp, and loud to chew.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: schweinshaxe
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole knuckle roasted for hours and basted with brown beer, until the rind becomes a shell that cracks under the knife.
